annotation.kind: direct formalization of Algorithm 3.1's positive exponential sum and equation (3.3)

assumptions: The dimension n is positive and x is a finite real input vector.
For every parameter value, each computed exponential satisfies wHat_i=exp(x_i)(1+delta_i) with |delta_i|<=u.
The computed exponential values are accumulated left to right by a StandardAddModel with the same nonnegative unit roundoff u and exact addition from zero.
The unit-roundoff family tends to zero, which gives the asymptotic meaning of the paper's O(u^2) term and eventually supplies every required gamma-validity denominator.
The real-valued relative-error certificates represent the paper's explicit no-overflow/no-underflow regime.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P14 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P14 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p14_t1_positive_recursive_sum_relative_error {n : Nat} (hn : 0 < n) {iota : Type*} {l : Filter iota} [l.NeBot] (x : Fin n -> Real) (u : iota -> Real) (run : forall t, P14BasicSumExecution x (u t)) (hu : Tendsto u l (nhds 0)) : positive exact sum /\ componentwise exponential bound /\ exists an O(u^2) remainder giving the eventual (n+1)u*s bound /\ exact additive error identity
formal_statement.plain_language: Algorithm 3.1's computed exponentials and their recursive sum satisfy the paper's (n+1)u*s+O(u^2) positive-sum error bound.

informal_proof: Bound each computed exponential by equation (3.1), apply the recursive-summation forward-error theorem to their exact sum, and combine the exponential and accumulation errors. Separate the linear term and show that all remaining terms are O(u^2) as u tends to zero.
informal_statement: The positive exponential-evaluation and recursive-summation analysis culminating in equation (3.3), with s, sTilde, sHat, DeltaS, the (n+1) coefficient, and O(u^2) all retained.
